verdicts.evidence: An independent numerical audit checks the supporting-score identity f(h)+(p-h)f'(h)≤f(p) for L1, L2, and KL on a 99×100 grid, yielding max oracle identity error 0, max constant-target score 0, and max supporting-plane violation 1.11e-16, confirming the constant 1-alpha predictor is unbeatable under perfect conditional coverage.

A deterministic re-aggregation of the authors' pinned 5,600-row results.csv yields LightGBM relative L1 power 68.929% vs PartitionWise 33.671%, close to the paper's 68.4%/38.3% and matching the current official notebook to <1e-5 percentage points; the qualitative gap is clearly supported though the PartitionWise value differs by ~4.6 points from the paper, likely due to code updates.

An independent synthetic experiment on the paper's 8D heteroscedastic model (theoretical L1 miscoverage 0.0948) shows L1-ERT rising from 0.0210 at 1k to 0.0866 at 30k test points (92% of truth), while unaligned CovGap falls from 0.0232 to 0.0049 (5% of truth), with oracle-group CovGap staying near 0.095.

The same 30,000-point synthetic run estimates over-coverage at 0.0445 (analytic 0.0460) and under-coverage at 0.0464 (analytic 0.0488), both nonzero and close to theory, confirming the asymmetric decomposition separates the two error directions.

Reading all 80 rows of the official released classification CSV confirms the additive identity between total KL-ERT and directional components (max residual 8.94e-8) and shows all 8 dataset/method groups have directional gaps >0.01 (e.g., CIFAR100/likelihood: 0.0852 vs 0.3234), though this is a released-output replay, not independent retraining.

A mutation control with 20 seeds, 2,000 observations, and 5 folds shows a label memorizer produces false in-sample L2-ERT of 0.08886 but cross-fitted null ERT of 0 (max train/eval overlap 0), while a genuine two-region signal is still detected at 0.01013, directly demonstrating that k-fold cross-fitting removes overfitting artifacts without erasing real conditional signal.

overall: The logbook provides concrete evidence for all six claims: four through independent experiments or mathematical audits (C1, C3, C4, C6) and two through deterministic re-aggregation of the authors' hash-pinned released outputs (C2, C5). The main limitations are that C2 and C5 are not independent reproductions, and C2's PartitionWise value (33.671%) differs from the paper's 38.3%, though the qualitative claim is strongly supported.
